 A pilot has issued a statement after online speculation suggested that she was on board the Learjet that crashed into a neighborhood in Florida on Sunday. Emily Shelton, a pilot who posts aviation-related content online, wrote in a story shared to her TikTok profile: "I was recently made aware that there are rumors that I was the pilot of the recent crash in Palm Beach." "I would like to respectfully clarify I was not." Shelton wrote. A spokesperson for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a statement to Newsweek on Monday morning: "A Learjet 60 crashed in a residential area near Cresthaven, Florida around 12:50 p.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1. Nine people were on board. The aircraft departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas." The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate, the spokesperson confirmed. The identities of the victims have not yet been made public. Shelton said in her statement: "I ask that people please stop speculating and spreading misinformation on this tragedy and be respectful of those involved. "My heart goes out to all those lost and affected," she added. Newsweek contacted Shelton for comment via social media message outside of normal business hours on Monday morning. In response to a request for comment on Monday morning, the Department of Transportation referred Newsweek to a statement issued by Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy on November 1. Duffy said that the crash was a "horrific tragedy." "Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost," he said. Newsweek also reached out to the Palm Beach Medical Examiner and Public Affairs for Palm Beach County for more information on the crash outside of normal business hours on Monday morning. Who Is Emily Shelton? Shelton, 22, is a pilot who shares content about her journey into aviation on TikTok, where she has more than 120,000 followers. Her name was linked to the plane crash amid rampant online speculation over who was on board the flight. The names of multiple female pilots have circulated in connection with the crash, but there is no evidence to support the claims circulating on social media at this time. Speculation extended to the passengers on the aircraft, with a viral rumor circulating on X that the musician Lenny Kravitz was on board. A representative for the singer told the local outlet BocaNewsNow: "The reports are untrue and incorrect." According to a TikTok shared by Shelton, she first began flight school in November of 2022, became a commercial pilot in 2023, and is seeking to become a corporate pilot in November of 2026. Shelton made headlines in August of this year after making an emergency landing in the middle of a Florida highway. While working as a flight instructor, Shelton was teaching an unnamed pilot-in-training who was on his first-ever lesson. The pair took off from Pensacola International Airport on the morning of August 3 in a 1974 Piper Cherokee Warrior light aircraft. They reached an altitude of 3,000 feet before dropping off tracking data. Dash camera footage later shared by Shelton on social media showed the plane later flying directly under an overhead highway sign structure before landing in the middle of Interstate 10. Shelton and the student were both able to walk away from the plane unharmed. The Florida Highway Patrol later said the plane had suffered an engine failure. Air traffic control audio from the incident captured Shelton reporting a smell of burning oil and declaring an emergency. “We would like to go ahead and declare an emergency,” she said at the time. “We’re losing our engine. I don’t know if we’re gonna make it to the airport.” What We Know About Sunday's Crash The aircraft came down near Cresthaven, which is around nine miles from President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. Images show a large crater in a multi-lane road, with fire and debris from the Learjet. No one on the ground was hurt. Air traffic control audio captured someone in the cockpit reporting “moderate turbulence” and that the crew was “managing the ice.” The person can be heard saying that the plane was “picking up precipitation” and saying “we need to climb.” The person then reported that the plane was descending at a rate of 10,000 feet per minute. An emergency was then declared, and the crew member is heard yelling, “We are in an overspeed condition, descending 20,000ft per minute,” and said, “We are going to crash into the ground.” Thirty-five seconds after the initial mayday announcement, a voice from the cockpit said, “We’re out of time.” Unverified video footage that has circulated on social media appears to be a dash-camera recording of the moment the crash occurred. That footage shows vehicles driving on a residential street when an aircraft suddenly nosedives into the ground and explodes. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told reporters at a news conference after the crash: “When you see that video, it’s a jarring thing. It’s like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere.” DeSantis said at the conference that, as of now: “We don’t have any reports of anyone who was on the ground… who was killed or injured.” Palm Beach County Fire Rescue has declared a “mass casualty incident.” What Happens Next The crash has caused significant damage to local infrastructure. DeSantis and local officials have said that 600 local residents were being evacuated from a nearby trailer-park community and officials have said it would be at least 30 days before the road is reopened. The FAA typically posts a preliminary accident/incident report the next business day after an incident occurs. Update 11/02/26 10:35 a.m. ET: This article has been updated with additional information. Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Rebecca Flood and Tony Phillips.
